identity.industry: Financial Services — Microfinance / Diversified rural NBFC (MFI + Housing Finance + MSME/Green Finance + emerging Tech & AIF units)

summary.oneLiner: FY26 was a recovery year — consolidated PAT up 79% YoY (Q4 alone +640% YoY, +125% QoQ) as credit cost normalized (FY26 3.8% vs 4.6% in FY25) and the sector passed its stress peak; management explicitly denies any one-off behind the Q4 PAT jump, attributing it to lower credit cost + growth. The diversification thesis is gaining traction — non-MFI AUM is 17% of consolidated book (target 30% by 2030) with Satin Housing and Satin Finserv each crossing ₹1,000cr AUM, prompting management to raise the FY30 consolidated AUM target from ₹25,000cr to ₹32,000cr.

one-line thesis: FY26 was a recovery year — consolidated PAT up 79% YoY (Q4 alone +640% YoY, +125% QoQ) as credit cost normalized (FY26 3.8% vs 4.6% in FY25) and the sector passed its stress peak; management explicitly denies any one-off behind the Q4 PAT jump, attributing it to lower credit cost + growth. The diversification thesis is gaining traction — non-MFI AUM is 17% of consolidated book (target 30% by 2030) with Satin Housing and Satin Finserv each crossing ₹1,000cr AUM, prompting management to raise the FY30 consolidated AUM target from ₹25,000cr to ₹32,000cr.

| Total revenue (consol) | ₹3,161cr | +23% | |
| PPOP (consol) | ₹928cr | +23% | standalone PPOP ₹856cr, +16% |

| On-book provisions | ₹273cr (2.9% of on-book book) | — | vs RBI-required ₹172cr; + ₹20.5cr management overlay |

| Credit cost (consol) | FY26 3.55%; Q4 2.2% (₹79cr) | — | |
| Cost of borrowing | 10.82% (marginal) | -43bps | funds raised in FY26: ₹10,826cr |
| CRAR (standalone) | 25.4% | — | 75 active lenders |
| Liquidity | ₹2,092cr balance-sheet + ₹2,235cr undrawn sanctions | — | ALM positive across all buckets |
> One-offs / items to normalize: management explicitly denied any one-off behind the sharp Q4 PAT jump ("no one-off… reduced credit cost and the growth strategy"). However, the P&L carries large, volatile non-core line items each quarter — net gain on derecognition of financial instruments (assignment/DA income) ₹144cr consol / ₹129cr standalone for FY26, and net gain on fair valuation (treasury income on mutual funds + forex contracts). Forex borrowing gains/losses are fully hedged and self-neutralize over time (FY25 had a net ₹25cr negative full-year impact); watch these lines for lumpiness quarter to quarter even though management says core NIM (13.5–14%) is stable.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue/AUM growth (FY27):** Standalone (JLG-only) AUM growth guided at 15–20% YoY, implying ~₹14,800–15,100cr; consolidated growth guided higher at ~25–30% (blending standalone 15–20% with SFL ~90% YoY and Housing ~38% YoY growth in FY26).
- **Margin:** Credit cost target 3–3.5% for FY27 (vs 3.8% actual FY26) — "meaningful improvement." NIM guided to stay stable at 13.5–14% (consol ~12–13%) even as non-MFI mix rises, because subsidiaries operate in the same high-yield rural markets (housing finance yield ~15.5–16%, Satin Finserv yield close to MFI levels ~25%).
- **ROA/ROE:** No explicit numeric guidance given; management declined to commit but indicated it "will be positive from where we are right now" (FY26 consol ROA 2.6%) when asked if >3% ROA is achievable in FY27 — treat as a soft aspiration, not firm guidance.
- **Order book / long-term AUM target:** Consolidated AUM target for 2030 raised from ₹25,000cr to ₹32,000cr, with non-MFI AUM target of 30% by 2030 (from 17% now).
- **Capex/expansion:** 392 new branches added in FY26 (total 2,015 branches / 577 districts); no major capex/commissioning items flagged (asset-light lending model).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable in the traditional sense (lending business); pipeline visible via disbursement growth (standalone disbursements ₹11,202cr FY26) and branch expansion (392 new branches added FY26, presence across 1 lakh+ villages, 550+ districts, 64% of India's pin codes).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Satin Housing Finance Ltd:** AUM ₹1,267cr, 3-year CAGR 36%; GNPA 3%; CRAR 53.8%; ICRA rating A- (stable). Customer mix: self-employed professionals + salaried; management sees the mix shifting further toward self-employed over the next 3–5 years. Average yield ~15.5–16%.
- **Satin Finserv Ltd:** AUM ₹1,054cr, +92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%; operates across 14 states / 121 branches. Secured lending (receivables, hypothecation of equipment, movable property; LTV ~40–45%) with zero customer overlap with MFI book (a customer must give up their MFI loan to take a subsidiary loan). Green finance book: ₹255cr disbursed across 34 loans (solar, EVs, renewable energy micro-enterprises); yield close to MFI levels (~25%).
- **Satin Technologies Ltd (STL):** Newly incorporated; builds enterprise tech (HRMS, loan management systems, core banking, cybersecurity) with agentic AI as a horizontal capability; acquired first 2 clients within 2 months of incorporation. Acquired a strategic stake in QTrino (IIT-Patna-incubated post-quantum cryptography deep-tech firm) in Jan-2026; has representative offices in Toronto and Dubai.
- **Satin Growth Alternatives Ltd (SGAL):** Received SEBI license for a ₹200cr Category II AIF — a gender-lens impact fund for rural MSMEs, led by an all-women team. Signed an MOU with State Bank of India for co-investment; progressing toward first close with "strong soft commitments."
- **Standalone net worth (₹3,129cr) exceeds consolidated net worth (₹2,868cr)** because of a historical (5–6 years ago, post-demonetization) revaluation gain booked on the parent's investment in subsidiaries at the standalone level, which is eliminated on consolidation.
growth verticals / optionality: Diversification into non-MFI rural financial services (housing, secured MSME/green finance, enterprise tech, AIF/asset management) is the core optionality thesis — management explicitly frames subsidiaries as "two kickers" to ROA: Satin Technologies (capital-light, high-leverage-of-knowledge business) and Satin Growth Alternatives (fee/AUM-based, capital-light asset management). Individual-loan JLG pilots are underway but management is clear JLG will remain the mainstay (hybrid, not a shift).
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **35-year institutional track record** navigating demonetization, COVID and the current MFI stress cycle — management cites this repeatedly as the reason for superior underwriting discipline and CXO team stability (avg. tenure >10 years).
- **Underwriting discipline evidenced in numbers:** sourcing-to-disbursement ratio of just 39% (reflects selectivity); borrower leverage policy caps at 3 MFI lenders / ₹2 lakh exposure; NATCAT insurance covering ₹5,800cr of disbursements since Sep-2025 to derisk against natural-catastrophe defaults.
- **Geographic risk management:** even in historically risky states, asset quality is now strong — Assam (once a risk state) PAR90 at just 0.7% with 100% collection efficiency; UP (largest state, 23% of book) PAR90 at 3%; Punjab 1.5%. All top states show 99.9–100% X-bucket collection efficiency.
- **Scale/reach barrier:** presence in 64% of India's pin codes, 2,015 branches, 577 districts, 34 lakh customers — a distribution network not easily replicated.
margins & cost dynamics: Consol NIM improved from 12.42% (FY25) to 13.23% (FY26) despite the non-MFI mix rising — management attributes this to subsidiaries earning higher-than-typical yields for their asset classes (housing ~15.5–16% vs standard HFC rates; Satin Finserv near-MFI yields ~25%) because they serve the same underserved rural constituency. Cost of borrowing declined 43bps to 10.82% (marginal), driven partly by ~50bps reduction efforts; management expects funding costs to stay stable-to-lower as repo rates ease. Reported average incremental yield on core microfinance ~25–26%.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Asset-light lending business — no major capex; expansion is branch-led (392 new branches in FY26) and subsidiary buildout (STL just incorporated, SGAL awaiting AIF first close). No slippage flagged.
capital allocation: Funding: raised ₹10,826cr in FY26 across 75 active lenders; maintains ₹2,092cr balance-sheet liquidity + ₹2,235cr undrawn sanctions, ALM positive across all buckets. Well capitalized — standalone CRAR 25.4%. SGAL's SEBI-licensed AIF (₹200cr target corpus, SBI co-investment MOU) represents a new fee-income/AUM-based capital-allocation vector outside the core balance sheet.
risks & watch-items:
- Forex/treasury P&L lines (derecognition gain, fair-value gain) are large and can swing quarter to quarter purely on timing/dollar movement even though fully hedged over the cycle (FY25 full-year net impact was -₹25cr) — watch for distortion in any single quarter's reported PAT.
- Sector-wide dependence on continued "healing" — PAR 1-180 days at 4.7% as of Jan-2026 (down from peak 6-7 months earlier); a reversal in disbursement growth or borrower overleveraging could reintroduce stress.
- Geopolitical/inflation risk flagged by an analyst; management's view is inflation upticks tend to increase credit demand over time rather than suppress it, but near-term income-level pressure was acknowledged.
- No explicit ROA guidance given — makes FY27 profitability trajectory harder to pin down precisely; investors should model off AUM growth + credit-cost guidance rather than a stated ROA target.
management quality / tone: Confident, data-dense tone from Dr. H.P. Singh, leaning on the 35-year track record and explicit avoidance of one-off explanations for strong results (repeatedly and directly denied any one-off when pressed by an analyst). CFO/Group Controller (Jugal Kataria) and CSO (Aditi Singh) handled granular numeric follow-ups (credit-cost splits, forex-line explanations) directly and transparently, including admitting inability to give a firm ROA guidance rather than over-promising.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Standalone net worth being *higher* than consolidated net worth (₹3,129cr vs ₹2,868cr) is a legacy revaluation-gain accounting quirk from a subsidiary investment revaluation 5-6 years ago — not a red flag, but worth knowing before comparing standalone vs consol leverage ratios.
- Management is deliberately not chasing the industry shift toward individual (non-JLG) loans — running only small pilots — while several peers are pivoting harder toward individual lending; this is a differentiated strategic stance worth tracking versus peer commentary.
- The ₹25,000cr → ₹32,000cr FY30 AUM target upgrade came purely from subsidiary outperformance (SFL +92.5% YoY, Housing 36% 3yr CAGR) — a tangible, quantified reason for raising the long-term target rather than a vague aspirational bump.

hero.oneLiner: FY26 was a recovery year — consolidated PAT up 79% YoY (Q4 alone +640% YoY, +125% QoQ) as credit cost normalized (FY26 3.8% vs 4.6% in FY25) and the sector passed its stress peak; management explicitly denies any one-off behind the Q4 PAT jump, attributing it to lower credit cost + growth. The diversification thesis is gaining traction — non-MFI AUM is 17% of consolidated book (target 30% by 2030) with Satin Housing and Satin Finserv each crossing ₹1,000cr AUM, prompting management to raise the FY30 consolidated AUM target from ₹25,000cr to ₹32,000cr.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Frames itself as the only MFI with multiple growth engines - an ecosystem of microfinance/MSME lending, housing finance, equipment and green financing, supply chain finance, tech solutions and an AIF - versus mono-line NBFC-MFI peers.
- Claims a 35-year track record across demonetisation, Covid and the recent MFI industry stress, with a 17% AUM CAGR over a decade and 20 consecutive profitable quarters.
- Counter-cyclical share gain: Satin's AUM grew 14% in FY26 while the industry contracted 13% (industry AUM fell to Rs 3,31,000 Crores after 8 straight quarters of decline), and active borrowers were stable versus a 23% industry decline.
- Benchmarks ahead of peer averages on FY26 NIM (13.6% vs 12.3%), 3-year AUM CAGR (19% vs 7.7%), GNPA (3.1% vs 3.4%), credit cost (3.8% vs 6.4%), ROA (2.5% vs 1.8%) and ROE (10.1% vs 7.4%).
- Deep customer franchise with ~34 lakh borrowers and 37%+ of borrowers having vintage greater than 3 years.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Satin Housing Finance Ltd:** AUM ₹1,267cr, 3-year CAGR 36%; GNPA 3%; CRAR 53.8%; ICRA rating A- (stable). Customer mix: self-employed professionals + salaried; management sees the mix shifting further toward self-employed over the next 3–5 years. Average yield ~15.5–16%.
- **Satin Finserv Ltd:** AUM ₹1,054cr, +92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%; operates across 14 states / 121 branches. Secured lending (receivables, hypothecation of equipment, movable property; LTV ~40–45%) with zero customer overlap with MFI book (a customer must give up their MFI loan to take a subsidiary loan). Green finance book: ₹255cr disbursed across 34 loans (solar, EVs, renewable energy micro-enterprises); yield close to MFI levels (~25%).
- **Satin Technologies Ltd (STL):** Newly incorporated; builds enterprise tech (HRMS, loan management systems, core banking, cybersecurity) with agentic AI as a horizontal capability; acquired first 2 clients within 2 months of incorporation. Acquired a strategic stake in QTrino (IIT-Patna-incubated post-quantum cryptography deep-tech firm) in Jan-2026; has representative offices in Toronto and Dubai.
- **Satin Growth Alternatives Ltd (SGAL):** Received SEBI license for a ₹200cr Category II AIF — a gender-lens impact fund for rural MSMEs, led by an all-women team. Signed an MOU with State Bank of India for co-investment; progressing toward first close with "strong soft commitments."
- **Standalone net worth (₹3,129cr) exceeds consolidated net worth (₹2,868cr)** because of a historical (5–6 years ago, post-demonetization) revaluation gain booked on the parent's investment in subsidiaries at the standalone level, which is eliminated on consolidation.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable in the traditional sense (lending business); pipeline visible via disbursement growth (standalone disbursements ₹11,202cr FY26) and branch expansion (392 new branches added FY26, presence across 1 lakh+ villages, 550+ districts, 64% of India's pin codes).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue/AUM growth (FY27):** Standalone (JLG-only) AUM growth guided at 15–20% YoY, implying ~₹14,800–15,100cr; consolidated growth guided higher at ~25–30% (blending standalone 15–20% with SFL ~90% YoY and Housing ~38% YoY growth in FY26).
- **Margin:** Credit cost target 3–3.5% for FY27 (vs 3.8% actual FY26) — "meaningful improvement." NIM guided to stay stable at 13.5–14% (consol ~12–13%) even as non-MFI mix rises, because subsidiaries operate in the same high-yield rural markets (housing finance yield ~15.5–16%, Satin Finserv yield close to MFI levels ~25%).
- **ROA/ROE:** No explicit numeric guidance given; management declined to commit but indicated it "will be positive from where we are right now" (FY26 consol ROA 2.6%) when asked if >3% ROA is achievable in FY27 — treat as a soft aspiration, not firm guidance.
- **Order book / long-term AUM target:** Consolidated AUM target for 2030 raised from ₹25,000cr to ₹32,000cr, with non-MFI AUM target of 30% by 2030 (from 17% now).
- **Capex/expansion:** 392 new branches added in FY26 (total 2,015 branches / 577 districts); no major capex/commissioning items flagged (asset-light lending model).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Diversification into non-MFI rural financial services (housing, secured MSME/green finance, enterprise tech, AIF/asset management) is the core optionality thesis — management explicitly frames subsidiaries as "two kickers" to ROA: Satin Technologies (capital-light, high-leverage-of-knowledge business) and Satin Growth Alternatives (fee/AUM-based, capital-light asset management). Individual-loan JLG pilots are underway but management is clear JLG will remain the mainstay (hybrid, not a shift).

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Consol NIM improved from 12.42% (FY25) to 13.23% (FY26) despite the non-MFI mix rising — management attributes this to subsidiaries earning higher-than-typical yields for their asset classes (housing ~15.5–16% vs standard HFC rates; Satin Finserv near-MFI yields ~25%) because they serve the same underserved rural constituency. Cost of borrowing declined 43bps to 10.82% (marginal), driven partly by ~50bps reduction efforts; management expects funding costs to stay stable-to-lower as repo rates ease. Reported average incremental yield on core microfinance ~25–26%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Funding: raised ₹10,826cr in FY26 across 75 active lenders; maintains ₹2,092cr balance-sheet liquidity + ₹2,235cr undrawn sanctions, ALM positive across all buckets. Well capitalized — standalone CRAR 25.4%. SGAL's SEBI-licensed AIF (₹200cr target corpus, SBI co-investment MOU) represents a new fee-income/AUM-based capital-allocation vector outside the core balance sheet.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, data-dense tone from Dr. H.P. Singh, leaning on the 35-year track record and explicit avoidance of one-off explanations for strong results (repeatedly and directly denied any one-off when pressed by an analyst). CFO/Group Controller (Jugal Kataria) and CSO (Aditi Singh) handled granular numeric follow-ups (credit-cost splits, forex-line explanations) directly and transparently, including admitting inability to give a firm ROA guidance rather than over-promising.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position
moat.body:
- **35-year institutional track record** navigating demonetization, COVID and the current MFI stress cycle — management cites this repeatedly as the reason for superior underwriting discipline and CXO team stability (avg. tenure >10 years).
- **Underwriting discipline evidenced in numbers:** sourcing-to-disbursement ratio of just 39% (reflects selectivity); borrower leverage policy caps at 3 MFI lenders / ₹2 lakh exposure; NATCAT insurance covering ₹5,800cr of disbursements since Sep-2025 to derisk against natural-catastrophe defaults.
- **Geographic risk management:** even in historically risky states, asset quality is now strong — Assam (once a risk state) PAR90 at just 0.7% with 100% collection efficiency; UP (largest state, 23% of book) PAR90 at 3%; Punjab 1.5%. All top states show 99.9–100% X-bucket collection efficiency.
- **Scale/reach barrier:** presence in 64% of India's pin codes, 2,015 branches, 577 districts, 34 lakh customers — a distribution network not easily replicated.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- Forex/treasury P&L lines (derecognition gain, fair-value gain) are large and can swing quarter to quarter purely on timing/dollar movement even though fully hedged over the cycle (FY25 full-year net impact was -₹25cr) — watch for distortion in any single quarter's reported PAT.
- Sector-wide dependence on continued "healing" — PAR 1-180 days at 4.7% as of Jan-2026 (down from peak 6-7 months earlier); a reversal in disbursement growth or borrower overleveraging could reintroduce stress.
- Geopolitical/inflation risk flagged by an analyst; management's view is inflation upticks tend to increase credit demand over time rather than suppress it, but near-term income-level pressure was acknowledged.
- No explicit ROA guidance given — makes FY27 profitability trajectory harder to pin down precisely; investors should model off AUM growth + credit-cost guidance rather than a stated ROA target.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Standalone net worth being *higher* than consolidated net worth (₹3,129cr vs ₹2,868cr) is a legacy revaluation-gain accounting quirk from a subsidiary investment revaluation 5-6 years ago — not a red flag, but worth knowing before comparing standalone vs consol leverage ratios.
- Management is deliberately not chasing the industry shift toward individual (non-JLG) loans — running only small pilots — while several peers are pivoting harder toward individual lending; this is a differentiated strategic stance worth tracking versus peer commentary.
- The ₹25,000cr → ₹32,000cr FY30 AUM target upgrade came purely from subsidiary outperformance (SFL +92.5% YoY, Housing 36% 3yr CAGR) — a tangible, quantified reason for raising the long-term target rather than a vague aspirational bump.

challenges.body:

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Consol PAT +79% YoY for FY26 (Q4 alone +640% YoY, +125% QoQ) on lower credit cost (3.8% vs 4.6% FY25); no one-offs per management despite large forex/treasury swing lines; non-MFI AUM at 17% (target 30% by 2030); FY30 consol AUM target raised ₹25,000cr → ₹32,000cr. FY27 guidance: standalone AUM +15-20%, consol +25-30%, credit cost 3-3.5%.
- _Q1 FY27 → check: credit cost trending toward 3-3.5% target; standalone AUM growth pace vs 15-20% guide; SFL/Housing AUM run-rate vs FY26 (~90%/38% growth); STL/SGAL traction (client wins, AIF first close); forex/treasury line volatility in the P&L; X-bucket collection efficiency holding at ~99.9%._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Satin Technologies acquired a strategic stake in QTrino Labs, a deep-tech quantum-safe cybersecurity company, in Jan'26 and held 68% as of 30 June 2026; FIPS certification is in progress and Big 4 channel partnerships are advancing.
- [Regulation] MFIN Guardrails 2.0 has reshaped the industry - 95% of industry exposure is now to borrowers with 3 or fewer active lenders - and NBFC-MFIs gained ~480 bps of market share as banks' share fell ~600 bps, creating a favourable mix for Satin.
- [Funding innovation] Secured a Rs 2,000 Crores direct assignment sanction limit from a PSU through what the deck describes as its first ever digital-direct assignment.
- [Credit rating] Standalone rated ICRA A (Stable) long term and A1 short term, with both SHFL and SFL at ICRA A- (Stable).
- [Group structure] Four wholly owned subsidiaries - Satin Housing Finance, Satin Finserv, Satin Technologies and Satin Growth Alternatives - form the diversification vehicle, with SHFL net worth Rs 381 Crores and SFL net worth Rs 344 Crores.
